title: 2026 National Day reception held at Taipei Guest House; attended by Eswatini King Mswati III and other foreign dignitaries
text:
On the evening of October 10, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) hosted the ROC (Taiwan) National Day reception at the Taipei Guest House, with Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung and his wife serving as the hosts. The event was attended by President Lai Ching-te, Vice President Bi-khim Hsiao, Premier Cho Jung-tai, Secretary-General of the National Security Council Jaushieh Joseph Wu, and other senior government officials. They were joined by foreign guests, including King Mswati III and Inkhosikati Make Zuma of Eswatini and members of the diplomatic corps and the diplomatic community, to celebrate Taiwan’s National Day.

To showcase the appeal of Taiwan’s everyday local cuisine and the diversity of its culinary culture, MOFA invited food and drink vendors from across Taiwan to participate in this year’s reception. Among the vendors were Wu Deng Jiang, Sinchao Rice Shoppe, Lin Jhen Kuih Shop, Yuciren, Chun Mei Ice Shop, and S.C Lab, which prepared a variety of classic Taiwanese dishes using fresh, seasonal, locally sourced ingredients and traditional cooking methods with creative culinary approaches.

During the event, President Lai accompanied King Mswati III and the Inkhosikati to the Wu Deng Jiang booth to sample traditional foods, including its signature braised pork belly rice and braised pork shank rice. The three then stopped by the Sinchao Rice Shoppe stand to taste its thickened soup with duck, mullet roe in a green garlic and apple sauce, and other dishes. After enjoying these savory dishes, they headed to Chun Mei Ice Shop to try desserts like almond tofu and bubble milk tea shaved ice. The dining experience enhanced Taiwan’s staunch friendships with friends from the international community through the common language of food.

Aside from these vendors of Taiwan’s local cuisine, the Chio-Tian Folk Drums and Arts Troupe and the Atayal Taiwan First Nation M-yu Dancers gave a joint performance that integrated traditional folk arts with indigenous dance and other elements and demonstrated the variety in Taiwan’s cultural heritage. The event also featured a performance by the Taipei Chanson Chamber Orchestra, showcasing Taiwan’s artistic soft power through a blend of classic and innovative music.

The official invitation to this year’s National Day reception, themed “Thirty Years of Democracy, Onward to the Future,” incorporated such elements as ballots, colored ribbons, and voting stamps. The main emblem combined imagery such as ballots and cascading ribbons, symbolizing the building of public consensus to propel the nation forward to a brighter future for its citizens. The 3D installation for the National Day reception had the theme “Majestic Peaks, Swelling Waves: Magnificent Taiwan.” It featured a silhouette inspired by the main peak of Jade Mountain. Through a rainbow of colors and vivid brushstrokes, the design portrayed Taiwan’s majestic mountain ranges and dynamic ocean waters, conveying Taiwan’s natural splendor, cultural diversity, and warm hospitality. (E)
